{
  "title": "The Keeper of the Decade",
  "world": "Cinematic Storybook Realism",
  "cold_open": "The heavy oak door groans against the winter wind, admitting a sliver of frost and a single, leather-bound spine.",
  "question": "How does a story stay so crisp, while the hands that hold it seem to remain frozen in time?",
  "journey": "For thirty years, the clock has struck the same rhythm. Every ten years, a man arrives. He wears a coat of charcoal wool, smelling of woodsmoke and old paper. He places the book—a nameless volume of maps—on the return desk. He doesn't speak. He simply nods. The librarian watches him through the glass. The man’s face is a landscape of gentle lines, yet his eyes possess the same clarity as they did in the seventies. The snow piles high, burying the world in white, while he stands there, an anchor in the shifting current of years.",
  "discovery": "The librarian finally opens the book. Tucked between the pages of the third chapter is a pressed wildflower, a blue cornflower. It is perfectly preserved, vibrant as if it were plucked only moments ago, yet the paper around it is yellowed and brittle.",
  "emotional_turn": "The man is gone before the door can swing shut. Only the scent of winter air remains. The librarian touches the flower and realizes it isn't a relic of the past, but a living heartbeat, a piece of a garden that no longer exists.",
  "payoff": "She looks at the date stamp on the return slip. It is today’s date. She realizes he isn't traveling through years; he is guarding a single, eternal moment, returning the map to the place where the story began.",
  "after_image": "A single blue petal falls onto the polished wood, settling like a quiet secret.",
  "hero_shot": "The man’s silhouette standing in the doorway, half-swallowed by the swirling white snow."
}
